subject: SDK field override: temporary priority routing for long-prefix POC
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@nexabank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SDK field override: temporary priority routing for long-prefix POC

Hi Sam / Nexa platform team,

Quick context: during the last two POC runs we've observed the Nexa demo requests that include a long policy prefix are being routed to a lower-memory variant and hitting streaming truncation / KV-cache misses. That causes the assistant to lose context mid-response and the UX fails the demo scripts.

Ask: can the runtime team enable a temporary "priority routing" escape for Nexa POC traffic so requests with header X-NEXA-POC: true are routed to the larger-kv-cache model variant for the next 72 hours? This is a short-term config change only — we want to avoid a full model rollout.

Why: the customer has an in-person demo Friday and we need a low-risk mitigation while Dev ships a patch later this week.

Constraints: Nexa requires that any special routing be auditable and rate-limited (they won't accept a global override). We'd prefer an API-header-based mapping to a pinned variant (no infra changes).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_nexabank.xlsx (current M.A.P.) and nexabank_map_mvp.pdf (example request shapes).

Requested next steps:
- Platform: confirm if header -> variant mapping is possible as a temporary policy (Karthik / Dev).
- Runtime: estimate risk and rollback plan if we need to revert quickly (Marissa / Dev).
- Sales/CS: we'll communicate scope to Nexa and lock demo time once we have alignment (Avery).

Thanks — please reply with feasibility and a suggested window.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@nexabank.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK field override: temporary priority routing for long-prefix POC

Avery / team —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick triage notes from runtime: the behavior you describe matches the KV-cache eviction + variant selection path where the router selects a lower-memory variant under certain sequence-length heuristics. Two practical mitigations we can consider immediately:

1) Header-based routing (preferred): allow a header (we can call it X-RW-PRIORITY or reuse X-NEXA-POC) that maps to a pinned variant with larger KV allocation. This is a routing table change only; we can limit by customer ID and rate.

2) Token-level prefix caching: we could enable prefix-preservation on the gateway for the Nexa route, but that's a heavier change and touches request-path caching.

For (1) I need:
- Example request IDs (sample traces) where it failed (Dev: can you pull 2-3 trace IDs from Nexa's demo runs?).
- Desired rate limit (Sam, what QPS do you expect during the demo?)

Risk: header -> variant mapping is low-risk but has a small chance of increasing memory pressure on the chosen pool. We'll need to set a soft quota per-customer and an automatic fallback if memory pressure > threshold. Rollback is trivial (remove routing rule).

I can prototype header routing as a dynamic routing rule and deploy to staging today. If staging looks good, we can push to prod in a controlled window.

I'll loop in runtime infra to propose a deploy window.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Platform Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@nexabank.com>

Subject: Re: SDK field override: temporary priority routing for long-prefix POC

Hi all,

Thanks — this is urgent for Friday's demo (we expect peak ~4 QPS during the live walkthrough, multi-region attendees). We prefer the header-based approach if it can be limited to the Nexa POC certificate and audited in logs. Compliance will need an audit record but won't accept any customer-wide permanent override.

Actionable: we'll add X-NEXA-POC: true to demo requests and can share a short whitelist of client IDs. We also need confirmation that the change won't affect other customers. Is rate limiting by customer ID + header feasible?

Happy to take a short call if that helps.

— Sam
Sam Lee
Platform Lead, NexaBank

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@nexabank.com>
Date: 2028-11-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK field override: temporary priority routing for long-prefix POC

Folks —

I dug into the sample traces Karthik asked for. Root cause: long-prefix requests sometimes cause the router's sequence-length heuristic to pick a smaller variant because the prefix tokens are treated as cold tokens in the runtime's heat estimator. When the main prompt continues, the KV cache misses and token generation truncates under streaming thresholds.

Proposed hotfix (attached hotfix_patch.diff):
- Add a short-circuit in the router: if header X-NEXA-POC:true AND customer_id in whitelist -> route to variant rw-v2-large-kv.
- Add a per-customer soft quota of 10 QPS for the mapping. If exceeded, requests fall back to default variant and a log event is emitted.
- Emit audit events to audit-log cluster / path: /audit/nexabank/poc-routing.

Rollout plan:
- Stage deploy to canary hosts Wednesday 18:00 UTC for internal tests.
- Prod rollout Friday 18:00 UTC (after Nexa confirms demo window), 10-min canary, health checks, automatic rollback on memory pressure (>85%) or error-rate spike (>1%).

I've attached hotfix_patch.diff and a short checklist in the patch header. The patch is small and runtime-local; rollback is a single config change.

Note long-term: we should address the heat estimator algorithm and consider prefix-aware warmup; I'll add a ticket. But this hotfix is low-risk and satisfies audit + rate-limit constraints.

Attachments: hotfix_patch.diff

— Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
